Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're finalizing procurement and need to establish how Redwood will invoice us for the upcoming pilot (Apr 2026). We have three legal entities that will be in scope: Horizon Health, Inc. (US), Horizon Health Europe B.V. (NL), and Horizon Health Labs Ltd (UK). The procurement team would like either: 1) a single consolidated invoice with per-entity allocation lines and VAT/TIN details included, or 2) separate invoices per legal entity.

Key asks from our side:
- VAT/TAX format: for EU services we need a reverse-charge style VAT line and the supplier VAT registration shown on the invoice. For the UK entity, please include the VAT registration number and the EU reverse-charge notation if applicable.
- Payment routing: Horizon Health (US) prefers ACH for the US entity and SEPA/IBAN for the EU entity. We would like one payment to Horizon Health, Inc. and internal reallocation — but we can accept separate wires if Redwood requires.
- Remit/PO: Please include a field we can populate with our PO number and remit instructions per entity.
- Pilot month billing: Can we start with a single consolidated invoice in Apr and iterate?

Attached a spreadsheet with our entity details (TIN/VAT placeholders). Can you confirm which invoice format Redwood recommends operationally and what you need from our side to set this up?

Thanks,

Hi Sana — appreciate the clear ask and the spreadsheet.

Short answer: Redwood supports both models and we typically recommend option (1) consolidated invoice with allocation lines for pilot phases to reduce AP friction, provided you can accept a single payer entity on the face of the invoice. Operationally:

- Option A (recommended for pilot): Single invoice to Horizon Health, Inc. with per-line accounting tags that map to each legal entity (we'll include VAT/TIN fields per line). Finance can produce a remittance advice CSV so your treasury team can allocate internally. Pros: simpler bank reconciliation for you; Cons: requires Horizon Health to own payment guarantee for the consolidated amount.

- Option B: Separate invoices per legal entity. Pros: clean legal separation and tax treatment; Cons: more invoices and potential cross-entity netting on your side.

What we need from you to enable Option A:
1) Confirm the payer entity (which legal entity will issue payment).
2) Provide final TIN/VAT numbers and preferred remittance bank details for each entity (your spreadsheet started this).
3) PO number format and any required invoice references.

I've attached our Redwood_MultiEntity_Billing_Guide.pdf and a draft quote (MA-Quote-6789.pdf) that includes sample line-item allocations and VAT formatting. Laura from Finance is CC'd to outline the accounting guardrails.

If useful I'd propose a 30-min call next week to walk through allocations and the DocuSign billing addendum.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Ops

Hi Sana / Markus,

Looping in a few process notes from Finance to avoid rework:
- If we issue a consolidated invoice we will populate per-line "entity_code" and "VAT/TIN" fields so your GL team can map rows to the proper legal entity. We can also provide a remittance advice .CSV with the allocation percentages/amounts.
- For accounting and audit purposes, when a single payer signs the SOW but multiple legal entities consume services, Redwood requires a billing addendum that clarifies billing risk and payment guarantee. This is a quick DocuSign and is purely administrative.
- With respect to withholding: Redwood is not a tax adviser — if Horizon requires gross-up or withholding handling we will need a signed agreement detailing who assumes the tax. We can include the invoice language (e.g., "Subject to withholding by payer") if that's the requested approach.
- Bank details: We will provide ACH/WIRE/SEPA details in the billing addendum (redacted here for security).

Please send the final TIN/VAT values and indicate whether Horizon Health, Inc. will be the payer for the pilot. Once we have that, Finance will provision the billing profile and we can start producing allocation-enabled invoices for Apr.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
